source_text: 冬至（Winter Solstice）是全年白昼最短、黑夜最长的一天，标志着一年中最寒冷时节的开 始。冬至过⌊，气温越来越低，人们的户外活动逐渐减少。农民地里活儿不多，主要忙于灌溉系 统的维护和农作物的防冻，同时为来年春天播种做准备。 中国人历来很重视冬至，许多地方都把冬至当作一个节日，庆祝方式各地不尽相同。北方人 有冬至吃饺子（jiao瀊i）的习俗，南方人有冬至吃汤圆（tangyuan）的传统。
reference_translation: The Winter Solstice is the day with the shortest daytime and the longest nighttime throughout the year, marking the beginning of the coldest season. After the Winter Solstice, the temperature gets lower and lower, and people's outdoor activities gradually decrease. Farmers don't have much work in the fields. They are mainly busy with maintaining the irrigation system and protecting crops from freezing, and at the same time, they are preparing for sowing in the coming spring. Chinese people have always attached great importance to the Winter Solstice. In many places, it is regarded as a festival, and the ways of celebration vary from place to place. People in the north have the custom of eating jiaozi on the Winter Solstice, while those in the south have the tradition of eating tangyuan.
